options.locationNote: 1415 Anthony Dr, Anthony NM, near I-10 exit 162 — approx coords; ~4-5 mi east of the day's NM-28/La Union endpoint (backtrack across the valley)
options.legalityNote: Established private RV park, tents welcome per listings
options.cyclistIntel: Restrooms w/ showers, laundry, WiFi; office hrs M-F 10-12 & 2-5:30 MST — call before arriving late
options.seasonalNote: Open year-round; late Oct lows ~45F in the valley

options.name: Gaslight Square RV Park
options.priceNote: Estimate only — small park, rates and tent policy unverified
options.locationNote: Approx coords, Vinton/Westway TX area off Doniphan Dr; OSM shows it 0.5 mi off route at mi 1837.4 (11 mi before day's end)
options.legalityNote: Private RV park; looks monthly/long-term oriented — tents unconfirmed
options.cyclistIntel: OSM-mapped only; no recent tent reports found in journals — treat as a maybe, not a plan

gapAdvice: Honest gap: the Anthony/La Union/Canutillo area has no true tent campground on-route. La Viña Winery (4201 NM 28, right at the day's endpoint) is a tasting room only — no camping offered (it does host an early-Oct wine festival; don't count on pitching there). Best plays: (1) call El Paso West RV Park and confirm a tent spot; (2) push ~15 flat miles up NM 28 to Mesilla/Las Cruces — Las Cruces has an active Warmshowers community and budget motels on Picacho Ave/S Valley Dr around $55-75; (3) motels cluster at the I-10 Anthony exit (~$55-70). Some riders simply combine this into a long day to Leasburg Dam SP (44 mi ahead, $20 guaranteed legal camping).

options.name: Leasburg Dam State Park
options.priceNote: Non-resident developed site $20/night ($15 NM resident) per 2025-26 fee schedule; W+E hookup sites add $15/day utility fees ($35 total non-res) charged even if unused — ask for one of the 5 non-utility developed sites. ReserveAmerica adds $3.50/night booking fee
options.locationNote: 12712 State Park Rd, Radium Springs — 0.1 mi off route at the day's endpoint
options.legalityNote: NM state park; fee schedule explicitly prices 'per vehicle, walk-in, or bicycle'
options.cyclistIntel: Classic Southern Tier overnight; 23 sites (18 W+E, 5 developed water-nearby), covered shelters, cactus garden. Reserve on newmexicostateparks.reserveamerica.com (6-mo window) or roll in for first-come sites — a solo tent on a Thursday in late Oct is low-risk
options.seasonalNote: Main comfort station + dump station were closed for renovation Feb 26-Aug 2026 — should be reopened by Oct 22 but call to confirm showers; vault toilets regardless. Late Oct: 75F days / 40F nights, superb

options.name: Sunny Acres RV Park
options.priceNote: Estimate; rates and tent policy unverified
options.locationNote: Las Cruces (approx coords, address unverified); OSM pins it near route mi 1875 — 18 mi before Leasburg, useful only if cutting the day short
options.legalityNote: Private RV park; tent acceptance unconfirmed
options.cyclistIntel: Backup only — Leasburg is the obvious play

options.name: Caballo Lake State Park (lakeshore primitive)
options.priceNote: Primitive/lakeshore camping $15 non-resident ($10 NM resident). Developed sites $20 non-res; W+E sites $35 with utility fees. Note: the 2026 drought fee waiver on primitive camping ran Aug 1-Sep 30 only — normal fees apply Oct 23
options.locationNote: Park entrance ~1 mi north of Caballo village on NM 187, just past the day's endpoint
options.legalityNote: NM state park; lakeshore primitive camping is designated and legal
options.cyclistIntel: 170 developed sites across 4 campgrounds (Riverside below the dam is the tent-friendly one, showers); lakeshore primitive is cheapest but exposed/shadeless. Pay station/office 7:30-4:30
options.seasonalNote: Watch goathead thorns — multiple reports of flatted bikes; keep to pavement, check tires

options.name: Percha Dam State Park
options.priceNote: Developed site $20 non-resident ($15 NM res); the ~30 W+E sites run $35 non-res with mandatory utility fees — ask for a non-electric riverside tent spot if available. +$3.50/night ReserveAmerica fee if booking online
options.locationNote: Off NM 187 ~4.5 mi south of Caballo village — reach it before the day's endpoint
options.legalityNote: NM state park, tent camping on developed sites
options.cyclistIntel: THE cyclist favorite on this stretch: giant cottonwood shade, grass, quiet, hot showers, riverside tent pitches, superb birding. 29 developed sites. Goathead stickers here too — walk the bike on dirt
options.seasonalNote: October is prime season on the Rio Grande; 75F/42F typical

options.name: Lakeview RV Park
options.priceNote: Estimate; tent policy and current rates unverified
options.locationNote: Caballo village on NM 187, at the day's endpoint (approx coords)
options.cyclistIntel: OSM-mapped; only worth a call if both state parks somehow fail (they won't)

options.name: Iron Creek Campground (Gila NF)
options.priceNote: Free per current USFS page; 14-day limit
options.locationNote: On NM 152 at ~7,300 ft, right at the day's endpoint on the west side of Emory Pass
options.legalityNote: Developed USFS campground, open year-round, no fee
options.cyclistIntel: ~10 shaded sites, tables, fire rings, vault toilet. NO potable water — load 5-6L in Hillsboro (last reliable store/cafe) or beg a fill in Kingston; creek water must be filtered. USFS flags flash-flood risk in the 2013 Silver Fire burn scar during storms
options.seasonalNote: COLD: late Oct at 7,300 ft means lows 25-35F, hard frost near-certain, first snowstorms possible — check the NWS forecast in Hillsboro before committing to sleeping this high; 20F-rated bag advised

options.name: Railroad Canyon Campground (Gila NF)
options.priceNote: Free per current USFS page (older flood-closure notices are stale — listed open year-round as of 2026)
options.locationNote: NM 152, ~1 mi west of Iron Creek (approx coords)
options.legalityNote: Primitive USFS campground, overnight use allowed, 14-day limit
options.cyclistIntel: Small primitive site at the Aldo Leopold Wilderness gateway; intermittent creek (filter). Overflow if Iron Creek is full
options.seasonalNote: Same cold warning as Iron Creek

options.name: Upper Gallinas Campground (Gila NF)
options.locationNote: North side of NM 152 between mileposts 26-27 (approx coords), ~2 mi west of Iron Creek
options.cyclistIntel: 3 sites, tables, vault toilet, no water. Lower Gallinas nearby is unverified (FS page 404s) — don't plan on it
options.seasonalNote: Same cold warning; slightly lower elevation than Iron Creek

options.name: Black Range Lodge (Kingston)
options.priceNote: B&B rooms, breakfast included — rates unpublished online (~$100-150 est); booking widget showed no rooms, so CALL. Historic cyclist-friendly stop; some tourers have been allowed to camp on the grounds for less — ask
options.locationNote: Kingston village, mi 1974.5 — 12 mi before Emory Pass, bail-out if weather turns
options.cyclistIntel: The warm-bed fallback before the pass; welcomes bikers per their site. If a cold front or snow is forecast at the pass, stop here and summit in the morning
options.seasonalNote: Kingston sits at ~6,250 ft — still frosty nights in late Oct

options.name: Gila NF dispersed camping (Burro Mountains)
options.priceNote: Free and legal on national forest land; 14-day stay limit
options.locationNote: Gila NF land flanks NM 90 around and past the day's endpoint toward Tyrone/Burro Mtns — pull off on forest roads (FR 851 area is a known dispersed zone); coords are indicative, pick any legal NF spot off the highway
options.legalityNote: Forest confirms 'millions of acres available for dispersed camping'; standard rules: camp off the road on NF land, 300 ft from water, pack out everything, verify no fire restrictions with Silver City Ranger District
options.cyclistIntel: Zero facilities — carry water from Silver City (routeMile ~2027). Confirm exact land status; private inholdings and the Tyrone mine property border NM 90
options.seasonalNote: ~6,000 ft: lows around 30F late Oct; fire restrictions possible in dry years — check before lighting anything

options.name: Burro Mountain Homestead
options.priceNote: $12/night tent without hookups + tax (on-season Apr-Oct, verified on their rates page); full-hookup sites $36.50+$3 electric
options.locationNote: 665 Tyrone Rd, ~4.9 mi off route from mi 2048.3 (6 mi past the day's endpoint) — approx coords, dirt/paved side road into the Burro Mtns
options.cyclistIntel: Best value with facilities on this day: $12 tent, restrooms, historic ranch setting; reviews describe a bathhouse but confirm showers when you call. No-refund window 48 hrs before check-in
options.seasonalNote: On-season rates through October; cool nights ~30F at 6,200 ft

options.name: Silver City KOA Holiday
options.priceNote: Tent estimate; recent reports $44-65/night (mostly RV) — tent sites w/ 20A electric typically run cheaper, call 575-388-3351
options.locationNote: 11824 US 180 E, ~6 mi EAST of Silver City between MM 118-119 — you pass it ~20 mi BEFORE the day's endpoint; only makes sense if ending the day short in Silver City
options.legalityNote: Established commercial campground with dedicated tent sites
options.cyclistIntel: Full-service (showers, laundry, WiFi); pool closed after Labor Day. Note: Silver City RV Park downtown (mi 2027.1) has PERMANENTLY CLOSED its tent area — don't route to it

gapAdvice: City of Rocks SP is ~25+ mi off-corridor east — skip it. Silver City is a Continental Divide Trail gateway town and generally friendly to dusty travelers, but it has no official free hiker/biker camp in town — the visitor center or Gila Hike & Bike (local shop) are the right places to ask about current CDT-er crash options if you want to overnight in town instead.

options.name: Veterans Park (City of Lordsburg)
options.priceNote: Free municipal overnight camping area, no fee, first-come
options.locationNote: South side of Lordsburg off the I-10 business loop, ~1.5 mi from route endpoint (approx coords)
options.legalityNote: City-designated free overnight camping — legal and normal; open all year
options.cyclistIntel: Gravel lot with shaded ramadas, tables, grills, dumpster — RV-oriented and no recent tent reports, but overnight camping is what it's for; pitch under a ramada. Water spigot has been reported OFF (Feb 2026) and no restroom confirmed — arrive with water and use town facilities. Reviews through Jul 2026 confirm it's active and free
options.seasonalNote: 4,300 ft: late Oct lows ~35F; I-10 and train noise

options.name: Lordsburg KOA Journey
options.priceNote: Tent estimate — allstays lists the park's tier at $41+/night (RV); 4 dedicated tent sites w/ water+electric, privacy fence, grill typically run low-to-mid $30s; call 575-542-8003 or 800-562-5772
options.locationNote: 1501 Lead St, 0.9 mi off route on the west side of town
options.legalityNote: Established commercial campground with tent sites
options.cyclistIntel: The comfort play after the Gila: hot showers, laundry, pool, tenter's sink, firewood on request. Clean and safe per reviews; expect I-10/train noise

gapAdvice: If the free gravel lot doesn't appeal after six desert days, Lordsburg's aging I-10 motels (Econo Lodge etc.) run ~$50-70 and the KOA's tent sites ~$35 buy a hot shower and laundry before the Arizona border.
